minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 22, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:02 p.m., on August 22, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 17, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths (arrived at 7:42 p.m.)
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Consideration of Initiation
  of Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.0. (Two
  Cases).

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d)
  of Section 54956.9) Troung v. City of Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  1  August 22, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two Closed Session matters for
which they provided direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

Item P8 was taken out of order.

P8.  Presentation on Chamber of Commerce Restaurant Week

  Doug Zielasko, Chamber of Commerce Chief Operating Officer, discussed Mission Viejo
  Restaurant Week and invited residents to check the list of 22 participating restaurants at
  www.mvrestaurantweek.org.

P1.  Recognize City Employees for Their Life Saving Efforts

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of recognition to City staff Sam Cho and Will
  Garcia and Tennis Pro Ryan Hill. Staff member Hsinyi "Jenny" Choy was unable to attend
  the meeting.

P2.  Saddleback College Presentation

  The City Council and audience received the presentation on the plans for a new Saddleback
  College athletics stadium and practice fields from Tim Jemal, President of the South
  Orange County Community College District Board of Trustees; Dr. Debra Fitzsimons,
  Interim Chancellor; Denise Whittaker, Acting President; Dan Clauss, Dean of Kinesiology
  and Athletics; Mark McElroy, Head Football Coach; and Mary Opel, Construction
  Manager.

P3.  Recognize the Mission Viejo Girls Softball 12U All Star Team "RELENTLESS" For
  Finishing 2nd Place at the Western National Championships

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of recognition to the coaches and players of the 12
  U All Star Team, Relentless.

City Council Minutes  2  August 22, 2017
 P4.  Recognize the North Mission Viejo Junior All Star Team for Winning the District 68
  Championship

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of recognition to the coaches and players of the
  North Mission Viejo Junior All Star Team.

P5.  Recognize the Viejo Little League 11 Year Old All Star Team for Winning the District
  68 Championship

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of recognition to the coaches and players of the
  Viejo Little League 11 year-old All Star Team.

P6.  Presentation on the Hearts for Hearts Foundation

  This presentation was postponed to a future City Council Meeting.

P7.  Presentation by Santa Margarita Water District on the National Award for the Lake
  Advanced Purified Water Project

  This presentation was postponed to a future City Council Meeting.

P9.  Mission Viejo Library’s 20th Anniversary - Save the Date

  The City Council received the presentation from Genesis Hansen, Director of Library and
  Cultural Services.

Presentation from the Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control (OCMVCD) Board of
Trustees

Dave Leckness, Member of the OCMVD Board of Trustees, reported on countywide vector issues
and noted that human contamination of West Nile Virus is lower than in previous years with no
reported cases in Mission Viejo.

P10.  A Mission Viejo Summer Review

  The City Council received the presentation from Grant Voss, Chairman of the Community
  Services Commission.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Speaking to agenda item #20, the following expressed concern with the possibility of a 241 Toll
Road extension through San Clemente and urged the Mission Viejo City Council to oppose a toll
road route through San Clemente and/or any of south Orange County: Aime Austin, San Clemente;
Laura Koneval, San Clemente; Randy Newkirk, San Clemente; Linda Williams, San Clemente;
James Wolfe, San Clemente; Karen Terry, San Clemente; Elizabeth Corder, San Clemente; Emily
Corbitt, Fullerton; and Michelle Schumacher, San Clemente.
City Council Minutes  3  August 22, 2017
 Wayne Brown, representing the South Orange County Economic Coalition: expressed support for
a north-south toll road solution to help solve traffic problems in south Orange County.

Brian Harrington, Oceanside: announced that he agrees with Mayor Pro Tem Sachs recent op-ed
where he stated that the Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA) study of toll road options should
continue and he said that Mr. Sachs represents Mission Viejo well on the TCA Board.

Don Wilder, M.V.: stated that Saddleback College has not been a good neighbor to the community
off Avery Parkway and he asked the City to do what it can to mitigate noise pollution, light
pollution and traffic during the stadium project. Regarding item 20 on the agenda, he expressed
opposition to any 241 Toll Road route that would affect the Coronado Homes in Mission Viejo.

Patty O'Connor, President of the Coronado Homeowners Association, M.V.: stated that the
Coronado HOA is concerned about the proposed alignments number 9 and 18 and how they would
affect their particular housing tract.

Dawn Urbanek, San Clemente: stated that she is speaking for the health and safety of students of
Tesoro High School because a road is being graded within 100 feet of the school. She said that the
Rancho Mission Viejo application for a drainage permit was done fraudulently.

*Council Member Raths (arrived at 7:42 p.m.)

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the Special City Council meeting of July 11, 2017, as
  presented, and (2) approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of July 11,
  2017, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated June 30, 2017 in the Amount of $504,008.64
City Council Minutes  4  August 22, 2017
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated July 7, 2017 in the Amount of $1,809,259.83

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated July 14, 2017 in the Amount of $655,871.74

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated July 21, 2017 in the Amount of $1,650,393.29

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Check Register Dated July 28, 2017 in the Amount of $973,590.21

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Check Register Dated August 4, 2017 in the Amount of $957,535.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

9.  Enhancements to Website Design and Content Management System

  Approved entering into agreement with and issuance of purchase order to 360 Civic in the
  amount of $40,900 + 10% contingency for website consulting and development.

10.  Advocacy and Government Relations Services on behalf of Successor Agency of the
  Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo.

  Approved the First Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with Joe A.
  Gonsalves & Son for advocacy services for a total not to exceed the amount of $47,500.

11.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2017

  Received and filed.

12.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2017

  Received and filed.

13.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June
  2017

City Council Minutes  5  August 22, 2017
   Received and filed.

15.  2017 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 18838)-Award of Contract

  Award the construction contract for the subject project to Roy Allan Slurry Seal, Inc., in
  the amount of $742,826.50

14.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for June 2017

  Received and filed.

16.  Comprehensive Bikeway and Transportation Connectivity Master Plan.

  Adopted Resolution 17-34 Authorizing the City Manager to enter into a Contract with the
  California Department of Transportation (CALTrans) (17-43A) for the Comprehensive
  Bikeway and Transportation Connectivity Master Plan.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

17.  Proposed Abatement of Weeds on Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed
  Abatement Program 2017 - Phase 2

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Bucknum opened the public hearing at 7:57 p.m. and with no requests to speak, she
  closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to instruct the
  Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in accordance
  with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

18.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Renovation CIP 14325

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  6  August 22, 2017
   Kris Yellin, Board Member of the Mission Viejo Nadadores Foundation, M.V.: on behalf
  of the Nadadores, she expressed support for the proposed contract amendment for the
  Marguerite Aquatics Complex renovation and thanked the City Council and staff for the
  smoothly run project and for the City's support.

  Council Member Sachs asked about the recommendation to install a shade structure which
  the City Council had not previously considered, and he expressed concern about going over
  budget.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to (1)
  approve Contract Amendment No 5. to Construct 1 One Corp., in an amount not to exceed
  $151,090.90 for unknown field conditions and site modifications, and (2) adopt Resolution
  17-35 Amending CIP 14325 Marguerite Aquatics Complex Budget by $157,000.00. with
  the exception of the shade structure and allocate the $10,000 that we are getting back from
  Bleacher A deletion and utilize that money for footings to install shade structure at a later
  time.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

19.  Cancellation of Special Tax Lien for Community Facilities District No. 92-1

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to authorize the
  Mayor to sign Notice of Cancellation of Special Tax Lien for the Community Facilities
  District No. 92-1 of the City of Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

20.  Resolution Supporting the Transportation Corridor Agencies’ Efforts to Identify a
  Balanced Solution to Relieving Regional, and Particularly North-South Traffic
  Congestion

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Bob Bunyan, M.V.: stated that mobility in South Orange County is an issue and he feels
  that citizens must look to the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) and the
  Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA) for solutions as they are the jurisdictional
City Council Minutes  7  August 22, 2017
   agencies. He said he supports the process that the elected officials must follow to obtain
  viewpoints and opinions from stakeholders throughout the region and to practice
  transparency while finding a solution that is mutually acceptable.

  Mark McGuire, San Clemente: expressed concern with the possibility of a 241 Toll Road
  extension through established communities in south Orange County.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the purpose of the proposed resolution is to poke at the
  San Clemente City Council and its citizens. She said the TCA's has not been a bastion of
  truth and integrity and its sole purpose is to make money for its investors.

  Sherry Clifford, San Clemente: stated that there has been inaccurate and inflammatory
  information circulating about her and she asked the Council to think outside the box to
  come up with an innovative alternative for true mobility solutions.

  Elizabeth Corder, San Clemente: expressed support for mobility but asked why the Council
  would aid the TCA which will be $4 billion over budget.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 17-36 to Support the Transportation Corridor Agencies in Solving Regional
  Traffic Relief in South Orange County.

  Council Member Raths said that the cities should work together to come up with a solution
  and he doesn’t think the resolution is necessary.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

21.  Ordinance Amending and Adding Various Sections to the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code relating to Administrative Appeals, Signage, City Manager Authority, Code
  Interpretation/Maintenance, City Commission Terms, City Property/Right-of-Way
  Use, Community Safety, Water Quality, Grading, and Animal Control

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  The following expressed opposition to the proposed changes in sections 13.04.050 and
  12.08.030 which, they said, will discriminate against the homeless: Eve Garrow, Policy
  Analyst for the ACLU of Southern California; Michael Robbins (no city of residence
  listed); Jeanie Robbins (no city of residence listed); Wes Jones, Anaheim, and Cathy
  Schlicht, M.V.

City Council Minutes  8  August 22, 2017
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to introduce
  Ordinance 17-324 Amending Sections 1.02.018, 1.03.018, 9.29.155, 9.29.220, 9.29.215,
  9.45.035, 2.08.060, 1.01.010, 1.01.005, 2.06.060, 13.04.010, 13.04.030, 13.04.050,
  12.08.030, 6.65.110, 8.10.600, 8.10.610, 14.03.020, 14.03.150, 14.03.330, 10.01.070,
  10.01.210, and 10.01.216, and Adding Section 14.20.90, Section 14.24.040, Section
  14.24.050, Section 1.01.171, and Division 4 Of Chapter 10.01, of The Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Relating to Administrative Appeals, Signage, City Manager Authority,
  Code Interpretation/Maintenance, City Commission Terms, City Property/Right-Of-Way
  Use, Community Safety, Water Quality, Grading, and Animal Control.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

22.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report and he asked for more information from staff
  or the City’s consultants before he takes a position and votes on SB 302.

23.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

24.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  This report was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

25.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  This report was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

26.  CUSD Ad-Hoc Committee Report

  City Manager Wilberg provided a summary of activity at Capistrano Unified School
  District within the last six months. He said the focus has been identifying how to utilize
  the money that is left in CFD 87-1 and redevelopment pass-through funds.

  Staff presented renderings of the proposed “STEM” science building at Newhart Middle
  School for which matching state funds may be available.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to approve the
  proposed letter to the CUSD Board of Trustees in support of the use of CFD 87-1 and
City Council Minutes  9  August 22, 2017
   redevelopment monies for the two proposed STEM classroom buildings at Newhart Middle
  School and Aliso Niguel High School.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS

27.  Support of Assembly Bill 1408 (Calderon) and Further Crime Legislation Reform

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 17-37 Supporting AB 1408, a State Measure To Require Revocation of
  Probation After a Third Violation; and, Promoting Legislative Reforms to Improve the
  Currently Unknown Unintended Negative Impacts of Existing Criminal Law.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC COMMENTS (Continued)

Ryan Farsai, M.V.: stated that City staff have made false statements to the Orange County Sheriff's
Department about him and his business partners. He said that the City illegally operates an LCD
sign on the premises of his ARCO gas station property and he has asked the City to pay $1,000 a
month to lease the property.

Julie Crandall, M.V.: expressed concern with the anti-camping clause added to the Mission Viejo
Municipal Code (agenda item 21.) She said that unless Mission Viejo has a place for homeless
people to sleep or find shelter, they should not criminalize camping.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

28.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

City Council Minutes  10  August 22, 2017
 Council Member Goodell

Due to the late hour, Council Member Goodell announced that he would defer his comments.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley highlighted recent events including Boots, Beer and Barbecue which
raised $5,200 to support the City’s adopted Marines; the super hero-themed Prelude in the Park
and Pacific Symphony concert; National Night Out sponsored by the Mission Viejo Police
Services department; two Drug Prevention Coalition meetings; and the 3rd Annual Night of
Remembrance for families who have lost children to a drug overdose. Council Member Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of August is self-control and she
provided a quote from Seneca: “Most powerful is he who has himself in his own power.”

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths apologized for being late to the meeting and announced that Orange
County Supervisor Lisa Bartlett is hosting a homeless issues roundtable at the Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center on September 6, 2017, from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs emphasized for residents that all five of the Council Members are heartfelt
about those in poverty and those without a home. He said it really bothers him when people come
to meetings and start accusing the Council Members of not having empathy for what is going on
in the community. He reminded residents that the votes that they make for State legislators have a
drastic effect locally because more and more, the State regulates what cities can and cannot do.
Council Member Sachs noted that Mission Viejo has great churches and synagogues that do
wonderful work. He said this is a giving, loving community with residents, Council Members and
staff who care and work hard to provide help.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum announced that throughout the summer, the City has been supporting Second
Harvest Food Bank and she reminded residents that September is Hunger Action Month. She
encouraged residents to volunteer at a food bank to see how the food is packaged and distributed
to those in need. Mayor Bucknum outlined her attendance at the City’s flag raising ceremony at
the Orange County Fair which, she said, was a lot of fun. She also participated in filming at the
Marguerite Aquatics complex to provide a video overview of the renovation project. Mayor
Bucknum referenced the earlier conversations about the 241 Toll Road and the residents who are
concerned about a proposal for the toll road extension to be built near the Coronado homes. She
noted that that particular proposal was offered by the City of San Clemente as a solution and she
has attended several regional transportation meetings where it was suggested that Mission Viejo
should handle the toll road extension. Mayor Bucknum said she will always advocate for Mission
Viejo residents and she will never stop. In closing, she read a letter from former residents who sold
City Council Minutes  11  August 22, 2017
 their home and moved to Lake Elsinore for retirement but wanted to express their thanks to the
City Council for making Mission Viejo a great place to raise their children.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:32 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of City staff member Deborah Carson, to
Tuesday, September 12, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 12, 2017

City Council Minutes  12  August 22, 2017
